newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Robotics, GoAmerica unveil wireless Web svc.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Robotics, GoAmerica unveil wireless Web svc.

text.p: U.S. Robotics Corp and GoAmerica Communications Corp on Monday unveiled plans to introduce a service that will give mobile computer users wireless access to the Internet's World Wide Web.

The Skokie, Ill.-based company's Mobile Communications Corp., a manufacturer of personal computer communications accessories, said its Allpoints PC Card will offer wireless access to the Web using a laptop computer. U.S. Robotics will utilize the GoAmerica service center application called Airbrowse, which supports such standard Web browsers as Netscape and Microsoft Explorer.
The two companies are demonstrating the new service at the COMDEX computer trade show this week in Las Vegas.

The cost of the service after the free two-week trial was not immediately announced, although GoAmerica said users will pay only for the transmitted information, not for connection time. Additionally, there are no telephone roaming fees, a factor that GoAmerica said will keep rates down. New Jersey-based GoAmerica is a national wireless service provider that offers wireless Web access, e-mail and specialized software platforms.
